errata.title_quirk: PDF title says 'Ensemble E2, E4, E8 Errata' but the scope section names E4, E6, E8 -- 'E2' is a transcription error in the source PDF title.

items.title: Clock pre-scale divider for RTC is incorrectly reset
items.consequence: POR_N assertion or STOP-mode wake resets the RTC clock pre-scaler divider while VDD_VBATT is sufficient.  RTC reverts to its default 32 kHz rate; the firmware-configured rate (typically 1 Hz) is lost.  Firmware can re-write the divider but the elapsed-time accuracy is gone.

items.title: RTC time drifts while POR_N reset signal is asserted
items.resolution: No fix planned for future silicon revision
items.consequence: While POR_N is asserted, the RTC clock source switches from the high-accuracy 32 kHz LFXO to the lower-accuracy LFRC (~5 % offset).  After de-assertion the source switches back to LFXO.  RTC accuracy drifts proportional to total POR_N hold time -- a 20 s POR_N assertion incurs ~1 s of RTC error.
items.workaround: Use an external real-time clock source if high accuracy is required

items.title: STOP mode current is higher than specification
items.consequence: Current entering VDD_BATT at 3.3 V in STOP mode is approximately 2 uA higher than the value specified in Table 5-5 of the E4 / E6 / E8 datasheets.  Reduces VDD_BATT battery life.
items.workaround: Use silicon revision A1, STOP mode current is as specified in the datasheet

items.title: External reset supervisor is required in some situations
items.resolution: No fix planned for future silicon revision
items.consequence: During the initial 10 ms cold-boot ramp at VDD_MAIN + VDD_BUCK, the supply voltage must rise monotonically and must never dip below 1.65 V once 1.65 V is reached.  Violations can permanently damage the SoC.
items.workaround: Use an external reset supervisor that drives POR_N active (low) while the supply is below 1.65 V.  See Alif Application Note AAPN0036 (PCB Layout Guidelines for Ensemble E4 / E6 / E8) for the reference circuit.

notes: 2026-07-25 DFP audit (Device/soc/AE822FA0E5597/include/), partially discharging the 'reconcile against v1.0' note above: spi_lp 1->2 (LPSPI0_BASE + LPSPI1_BASE -- the old 1 was wrong on the part we bench), and dma_general_32ch added as 3 (DMA0/DMA1/DMA2, each with _NS and _SEC views) -- the key was simply missing here while E4/E6 already carried it.  Every other count in this block was re-verified against the DFP base symbols and soc_features.h and is correct.

Datasheet re-pointed to ADTS0013 v1.2 (June 2026) on 2026-08-30, from v1.0 (#1811).  active_ua_per_mhz corrected 29 -> 27: 29 traced to the pre-1.0 Alif E8 Datasheet 0.51 draft, while v1.2 Features reads 'As Low as 27 uA/MHz Dynamic Consumption for High-Efficiency Cortex-M55'.  vin_v added as 1.75-4.8 V (Features, '1.75 V to 4.8 V Primary Supply Range'; Table 5-4 note 5 requires VDD_MAIN and VDD_BUCK tied together).  Peripheral counts were re-verified against the DFP in the 2026-07-25 audit above and are not re-derived here.

I2C ceiling is 1.0 Mbps, not 3.4 Mbps: v1.2 Features reads '4x I2C Channels up to 1.0 Mbps Throughput', and Table 9-1 records 'Updated I2C throughput from 3.4 Mbps to 1.0 Mbps in Section Features, Section 3.17.4 I2C Overview, and Table 5-3' plus 'Removed HS mode column ... in Table 5-30 I2C Timing Characteristics'.  I2C High-Speed mode is therefore no longer a specified capability on this part.  Not encoded as a field because soc-spec-v1 has no per-bus throughput ceiling, so a board.yaml asking for a faster clock-frequency still passes validation (#1811).

spi_lp = 2 counts REGISTER BLOCKS, not usable buses.  v1.2: 'Up to two Low-Power SPI modules (LPSPI0 and LPSPI1) in the RTSS-HE, sharing device pins and thus forming a single LPSPI channel', with master mode only on LPSPI0 and slave mode only on LPSPI1.  The count stays 2 to match the DFP base symbols (2026-07-25 audit note above); a consumer must not read it as two independent buses (#1811).

power.stop_ua = 1.3 is a single scalar over what Table 5-5 defines as STOP_0 through STOP_5, each with a different retention set, a different typical current and separate retention adders.  soc-spec-v1 cannot express that ladder; the number is kept as the best single figure and must not be read as the current in any particular STOP mode (#1811).
HWRM v0.3 is Alif-confidential -- referenced here for traceability; the file itself stays out of git.
Errata AERR0012 v2.0 covers E4/E6/E8 jointly; individual `items` list is pending ingestion against the errata doc.
E8 adds 1× Ethos-U85 NPU (Generative AI, supports Transformers) on top of the E7 NPU pair.
E8 swaps OctalSPI for HexSPI (16-bit, 400 MB/s SDR / 800 MB/s DDR) -- a different external-memory protocol than E3/E7.
E8 ships an ISP and JPEG encoder (E3/E7 do not).
WLCSP216 package exposes 136× 1.8-V GPIOs; FBGA194 exposes 120 (note: 'GPIO[0-14]' subset on FBGA per datasheet table 7-1).
AE822FA0E5597LS0 is the variant Alp Lab uses on the E1M-AEN801 module SKU.
USB = xHCI USB-2.0 dual-role @ 0x48200000 (IRQ 101), 16 endpoints; grounded from the Alif DFP soc.h/soc_features.h (AE822FA0E5597). Host mode supported.

debug.expect_dpidr = 0x4C013477 on AE822FA0E5597LS0 is a MEASUREMENT, not a derivation (#1355): re-confirmed on real silicon 2026-08-10 (`Found SW-DP with ID 0x4C013477`), and independently recorded across docs/bring-up-aen.md, docs/debugging-aen.md, docs/aen-provisioning.md, docs/aen-bench-bringup.md and docs/_aen-runbook-section.md, plus scripts/bench/aen/bench-env.sh's AEN_DPIDR default.  It is set for the single remaining variant; the AE822FA0E5597BS0 (WLCSP216) row this note used to contrast against was dropped by #1444, and validate_metadata.py::_check_soc_no_wlcsp_variants now refuses to let it back in.  The rule that contrast existed to state still holds generally: never arm expect_dpidr from a same-family assumption -- an unarmed guard is recoverable, a guard armed at the wrong ID passes on the board it exists to exclude.  (The WLCSP216 entries at `packages` and the GPIO-count note above are vendor facts about the silicon, not variant rows, and stay.)
